statement: If G has no even cycle, every choice of frequencies and nonzero symmetric edge couplings retains the full adjacency-polytope count of complex torus roots, counted with multiplicity.

answer.display: No loss of torus-root multiplicity when G has no even cycle
answer.text: The exceptional coupling set for failure of Bernshtein generality is empty on this graph subclass.

scope: Connected graphs without even cycles; arbitrary real or complex frequencies and nonzero symmetric couplings.
notes: All torus roots remain isolated. Multiple roots may still occur, so this does not assert that the ordinary discriminant is empty. Trees retain 2^(N−1) roots and odd N-cycles retain N·binom(N−1,(N−1)/2), with multiplicity.
